packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-01 — unverified image reading (first reader, rerun)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. I read only the brief, PROMPT.md and the packet images (plus crops of them).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, face A)
- Photograph shows FIVE separate parchment fragments laid side by side on black, with colour checker and a cm ruler; two plastic weights at top/bottom between fragments 2 and 3. All appear upright.
- Fragment 1 (leftmost, ~7 x 12 cm): heavily abraded/faded, a vertical fold/crease down the middle; small brown text in long lines with scattered red strokes (rubricated paragraph marks / capital touches) at line ends on the right. A modern pencil note in the lower centre.
- Fragment 2 (~7 x 12 cm): red decorated initial (looks like a Lombard-style letter) at top centre; many lines of small dark brown text, very rubbed; red paragraph strokes in margins left and right. Modern pencil note bottom right.
- Fragment 3 (narrow strip, ~2.5 x 12 cm): mostly blank or very faded; modern pencil shelfmark written vertically; a red mark near lower right.
- Fragment 4 (~5 x 12 cm): text in a larger hand, lines cut at the right edge; red touches; modern pencil note written vertically at right.
- Fragment 5 (rightmost, ~7 x 12 cm): largest and clearest script (proto-gothic/gothic book hand), single column, red initial at top left (C/G?) and a large red initial B mid-column; red rubrication; heavy damage/flaking in lower half.
- These are tentative observations; whether the fragments come from one book is not determinable from the overview alone.
- Tiles image-002..009 are native-resolution tiles of this face (4 across x 2 down, overlapping).

TILE image-002 (upper half of fragment 1; at far right the left edge of fragment 2)
- Fragment 1 surface is severely abraded and faded; a vertical fold runs down the centre. Ink is pale brown; red horizontal strokes (line-fillers or paragraph/rubric strokes) at about y=315, 490, 745 (right side) and y=500, 750 (left side) in tile coordinates.
- Viewed natively and with a contrast-stretched greyscale crop (crops/packet-01/002-enh.jpg). Letter shapes are visible but I could not resolve any word with confidence. Short lines in the right half (x~680-1000) look like the ends of lines in a small minuscule; isolated letter groups only.
- Tentative glimpses only (not reliable): image-002 l.~ (y≈330) "...e agi..?" ; (y≈620) "...[illegible] p(ro)?..." . I record nothing as a reading.
- Limitation: this face of fragment 1 is effectively illegible at this resolution/lighting; UV or multispectral imaging would be needed.
- Fragment 2 left edge (x>1260): red paragraph marks at y≈430, 680, 865; text cut by tile edge — read on image-003.

TILE image-003 (upper part of fragment 2; at right, upper part of fragment 3 strip)
- Fragment 2: red Lombard-type initial at x≈400-580, y≈170-350 (letter form uncertain: looks like an N/H-like shape with a hollow left bow; could also be a reversed/mirrored letter). Red horizontal strokes (line-fillers/paragraph strokes) at y≈290 (left of initial), 300 (right), 410 (right margin), 425 (left margin, with a red cross-like mark), 675, 865, 915.
- Text: ~22 lines visible in this tile, small brown minuscule, very rubbed, also a vertical crease at x≈790. Contrast-stretched crop (crops/packet-01/003-enh.jpg) did not make words readable.
- OBSERVATION worth checking: the letter shapes look as if they might be mirror-written, i.e. an offset (set-off) of text from a facing page rather than the scribe's ink, or the image is of a face carrying transferred ink. I made a mirror test crop (crops/packet-01/003-mirror-test.jpg: top = as photographed, bottom = mirrored). Neither orientation gave me a confident word. In the mirrored version, the first line of the crop superficially suggests "...[illegible] comm[illegible]..." — NOT a reliable reading.
- No line of fragment 2 on this tile is transcribed; all [illegible].
- Fragment 3 (strip, x>1330): no text visible in upper part; a modern pencil note begins at bottom right (x≈1430, y≈940-1040), vertical.

TILE image-004 (fragment 3 lower-right edge at left; upper ~80% of fragment 4 at x≈680-1340)
Crops: crops/packet-01/004-frag4-0.jpg (y 50-560, x2) and 004-frag4-1.jpg (y 540-1040, x2).
Layout observations, fragment 4: single column, cut at left (line beginnings lost) and with a blank right margin carrying a modern pencil note ("Stams? ... 33-24"?, vertical). Lines of two sizes: larger formal gothic text lines alternate with smaller lines; several of the small lines consist of scattered strokes/dots that look like NEUMES above text lines (observation; interpretation tentative: a noted liturgical book). Red rubrics: a red "R" with abbreviation stroke (responsory sign?) and a red "V"-like sign (versicle?), a red rubric line "...laudes".
Fragment 3 (strip, x<340): faint traces at its right edge x≈300-340 (y≈530, 690, 820, 970), probably line-ends/beginnings: "d", "q"?, "b"? — not readable as words. Modern pencil "33-34"? at bottom left (vertical).

Fragment 4 transcription (line numbers counted from top of image-004; y = approx.):

004 l.4  (y≈240) [..]nane? riren? ex. Q(uod)?/S? lingua   [small/medium script; "ex." and "lingua" fairly clear; the letter before "lingua" is a tall ligature/abbreviation, unresolved]
004 l.5  (y≈320) [..]re n(on)? audet: so[..]       [larger; "audet" with stroke over preceding a/n — written "nāudet"; could be "n(on) audet" or "na(m) audet"]
004 l.6  (y≈410) [.]a(m)? aude? sidiā p[..]      [larger; letters "audesidia" then abbreviation stroke over final a, then p + abbreviation; word division uncertain: "a(m) desidia(m) p(er)?" or "aude(n)s? id..."]

004 l.11 (y≈780) [..]onorum? uthano? nob(is)? am?[..]   [medium; uncertain]

004 l.13 (y≈860) [..]s q(ui)? lyre? loc?, [red ⁊/V-sign] V? or d? lyre?[..]   [small; uncertain]
004 l.14 (y≈945) [red rubric:] [.]laudes. A? [red]   ["laudes" clear in red; first letter cut/damaged; red letter after point]
004 l.15 (y≈1000) [neume-like strokes / faded; illegible]
- Lower part continues on image-008.

TILE image-005 (left: lower-left edge of fragment 4 strip-margin, no text; right: upper ~80% of fragment 5)
Crops: crops/packet-01/005-0.jpg (y 20-420), 005-1.jpg (y 400-800), 005-2.jpg (y 780-1042), all x 520-1488, x1.4.
Layout, fragment 5: single column, right edge cut (line-ends lost), left margin intact with modern pencil note written vertically ("Stams, Stift, Frag. 33-1a"? — modern, uncertain). Red decorated initial (C/G-shaped, with internal red dot/flourish) at top left, x≈530-670, y≈20-130. Large red initial B (Romanesque/early gothic, ~3 lines high) at x≈500-660, y≈650-850. Red small "A"-like sign after "filio." (y≈595) and a red P-like letter at the right edge (y≈820-880). Main text in a regular gothic/proto-gothic book hand of medium size; after the B-initial the text becomes smaller with lines of neume-like marks above (observation; interpretation tentative: notated chant text).

Transcription, fragment 5 (lines counted from top of image-005):
005 l.1  (y≈90)  [red initial C/G?] lium. et sp(iritu)m s(an)c(tu)m. unum d(eu)m om(n)ip[...]      ["lium" — the first letter is the red initial; ending "omip"/"omnip" cut]
005 l.2  (y≈190) tentem. uni(us) sub(stanti)ȩ? uni(us) potestatis. crea[...]   [superscript "9"-shaped -us signs over "uni" twice; "subē" with abbreviation stroke = my expansion "substantie" is a guess from the abbreviation, the letters are "sub" + e-with-hook/stroke]
005 l.3  (y≈275) omnium creatura(rum)? . Credimus p(at)rem[...]   ["creatura" + a -rum/ꝝ-like flourish under final a; "patrem" abbreviated with stroke]
005 l.4  (y≈355) ñ? nabitio?. filium a patre genitum. d(eu)m ue[...]   [first word uncertain: tilde-n then "nabitio" or "natiuio"?; "filium a patre genitum" clear; "dm" with stroke then "ue"/"ui" cut]
005 l.5  (y≈430) de d(e)o. lumen [.]um d(e)? lumine? [illegible] [...]   [faded/rubbed middle; "de do" with stroke; "lume(n)" fairly clear; rest uncertain]
005 l.6  (y≈515) a patre et filio equal(ite)r? p(ro)cedent[em?] [...]   ["a patre et filio" clear; "equal..." then p with stroke "p(ro)cedent.."; right end damaged]
005 l.7  (y≈600) tem. coȩt(er)num? p(at)ri ⁊ filio. [red A-like letter]   ["tem" (end of previous word); "coaeternum"? letters c o ? t ? n u m with an abbreviation; then "patri" abbreviated? "⁊ filio." clear]
005 l.8  (y≈650) [neume-like marks]
005 l.9  (y≈705) [red B initial] [.]enedictio? no? deus? de? [illegible]   [small script, very faded; reading quite uncertain]
005 l.10 (y≈740) [neume-like marks]
005 l.11 (y≈785) [.]mam? cum omni? fine?   [small script; uncertain]
005 l.12 (y≈820) [neume-like marks] ... [red P at right edge]
005 l.13 (y≈870) [..]uiseramur? ut? a? ue? [illegible] ue? [illegible]   [small script; very uncertain; flaking]
005 l.14 (y≈960) p(?)manis? d(eu)s? in? c[.]sta? s? pl[...] [illegible: flaking]   [medium script; uncertain]
005 l.15 (y≈1030) [top of a line, cut by tile edge; read on image-009]
- Damage: scattered flaking of the surface in the right half from y≈550 down; text under flakes lost.

TILE image-006 (lower half of fragment 1; at right, left edge of fragment 2 lower part)
- Fragment 1 lower half: same faded, abraded surface; a red paragraph/initial stroke (L-shaped red mark) at x≈50-195, y≈240-300; another red stroke at x≈800-860, y≈715 and x≈920-980, y≈485. A diagonal crease/fold line runs from x≈880,y≈470 to x≈470,y≈870. Modern pencil note at x≈390-560, y≈400-490: "STA, Frag. 33-5a"? (modern; uncertain).
- Crops: crops/packet-01/006-right-blue.jpg (blue channel, contrast-stretched, x2) and 006-orient-test.jpg (same area mirrored / rotated 180 / flipped). The letter forms (bowed "g/q"-like shapes, many descenders) did not resolve into words in any orientation. I therefore cannot say whether this face's writing is direct ink, an offset, or simply faded; none of it is transcribed.
- All lines of fragment 1 on this tile: [illegible].
- Fragment 2 left edge (x>1240): ~25 line-beginnings, faded; red stroke at y≈45 and y≈610; not readable on this tile.

TILE image-007 (lower part of fragment 2; at right, lower part of fragment 3 strip)
- Fragment 2: ~30 lines of small minuscule, faded and rubbed; red line-filler/paragraph strokes at x≈480-610,y≈97; x≈90-135,y≈45; x≈870-950,y≈435; x≈750-860,y≈555; x≈110-150,y≈612; x≈880-1010,y≈852. A faint vertical ruling/crease near x≈610 and another near x≈830 (could indicate two narrow columns or just folds; not decidable). Modern pencil at bottom: "STA, Frag. 33.4a"? (uncertain).
- Contrast crop of lower left (crops/packet-01/007-lowleft.jpg, blue channel x2): darkest line (tile y≈850) shows a word looking like "[.]an?lu?ac?o" / "consolacio?" — NOT reliable; I do not offer it as a reading.
- No line of fragment 2 transcribed: [illegible] throughout at this resolution.
- Fragment 3 strip (x≈1330-1647): mostly blank; modern pencil note vertical "Stams, STA, Frag. 33-3a"? (uncertain); at the far right edge (x>1590) traces of letters and a red mark (y≈540-580) and red at y≈930 — these belong to text continuing beyond the strip's right edge and are only 1-2 letters wide; illegible. Holes at y≈750-820, 870-910.

TILE image-008 (left: lower fragment 3 strip; right: lower part of fragment 4) — overlaps image-004 by ~1 line (the "...q lyre loc, [red] V..." line and the red "laudes" rubric appear at top of image-008; not counted twice)
Crops: crops/packet-01/008-frag4.jpg (x 670-1150, y 90-800, x1.8); crops/packet-01/008-frag3edge.jpg (x 240-350, y 80-940, x2).
Fragment 3 strip: at its right edge, beginnings of lines of a gothic text (larger script) cut by the strip edge, one or two letters each, with a red flourished initial/sign (≈y 545-570) and red at the bottom (≈y 920). Visible letters top→bottom: "b", "u", "[.]m", "og?/ag", [red sign], "I?/u", "go?/ge", "[.]". Not words; recorded only.
